3754.d: Neuter of hostis as conjunction; demonstrative, that; causative, because.

3029.d: Very; very much, exceedingly, greatly. Of uncertain affinity; much.

3816.d: A boy, or, a girl, and a child; specially, a slave or servant.

3870.d: To call near, i.e. Invite, invoke.

3962.d: Father, (Heavenly) Father, ancestor, elder, senior. Apparently a primary word; a |father|.

3192.d: Honey. Apparently a primary word; honey.

3971.d: Hereditary, received from fathers. From pater; paternal, i.e. Hereditary.

3147.d: To flog, scourge, whip. From mastos; to whip.

3891.d: To act contrary to law. From a compound of para and nomos; to be opposed to law, i.e. To transgress.

3079.d: Claudius Lysias, a Roman tribune of the soldiers in Jerusalem. Of uncertain affinity; Lysias, a Roman.

3839.d: In every way, entirely, everywhere. Adverb from pas; wholly.

3116.d: With longsuffering, patiently. Adverb of a compound of makros and thumos; with long temper, i.e. Leniently.

3987.d: Mid: I try, attempt, endeavor. From peira; to test, i.e. to attempt.

3805.d: Destined to suffer. From the same as pathema; liable to experience pain.

3130.d: Raving madness, frenzy, insanity. From mainomai; craziness.

3697.d: Of what kind that, i.e. How great.

3460.d: Myra, a port in Lycia, south-west Asia Minor. Of uncertain derivation; Myra, a place in Asia Minor.

3073.d: Lycia, a province of Asia Minor.

3881.d: To coast along, sail along. From para and the middle voice of lego;, to lay one's course near, i.e. Sail past.

3040.d: A harbor, port, haven. Apparently a primary word; a harbor.

3867.d: To admonish, advise, exhort. From para and aineo; to mispraise, i.e. Recommend or advise.

3490.d: A captain (master) of a ship, ship-owner. From naus and kleros; a captain.

3915.d: Wintering, spending the winter. From paracheimazo; a wintering over.

3914.d: To pass the winter. From para and cheimazo; to winter near, i.e. Stay with over the rainy season.

3047.d: The south(- west) wind (as bringing rain, i.e. the south quarter).

3519.d: A little island, an islet. Diminutive of nesos; an islet.

3492.d: A sailor, seaman. From naus; a boatman, i.e. Seaman.

3712.d: A fathom, about five or six feet. From oregomai; a stretch of the arms, i.e. A fathom.

3491.d: A ship, vessel. From nao or neo; a boat.

3194.d: Melita, now Malta. Of uncertain origin; Melita, an island in the Mediterranean.

3328.d: To change; mid: I change my mind. From meta and ballo; to throw over, i.e. to turn about in opinion.

3902.d: Marked with; a figure-head. From para and the base of semaino; side-marked, i.e. Labelled (figure-head) of a ship).

3578.d: Lodging, hospitality. From xenos; hospitality, i.e. a place of entertainment.

3410.d: A rented house, hired dwelling. From misthoo; a rented building.

3417.d: Remembrance, recollection, mention; commemoration. From mnaomai or mimnesko; recollection; by implication, recital.

3154.d: To become vain or foolish, be perverted. From mataios; to render foolish, i.e. wicked or, idolatrous.

3337.d: To change, transform, alter, exchange. From meta and allasso; to exchange.

3806.d: Suffering, emotion, depraved passion, lust. From the alternate of pascho; properly, suffering, i.e. a passion.

3715.d: Strong desire, lust, appetite. From oregomai; excitement of the mind, i.e. Longing after.

3115.d: Patience, forbearance, longsuffering. From the same as makrothumos; longanimity, i.e. forbearance or fortitude.

3053.d: Reasoning, thinking; a conception, device. From logizomai; computation, i.e. reasoning.

3810.d: An instructor, trainer; almost: a chastiser. From paideuo; a trainer, i.e. Teacher or discipliner.

3446.d: Form, outline, semblance. From morphoo; formation, i.e., appearance (concretely) formula).

3847.d: A transgression, overstepping, deviation. From parabaino; violation.

3848.d: A transgressor, law-breaker. From parabaino; a violator.

3691.d: (a) sharp, (b) swift, eager. Probably akin to the base of akmen; keen; by analogy, rapid.

3929.d: Overlooking, suspension, remission of punishment for. From ktetor; praetermission, i.e. Toleration.

3108.d: Regarding as happy, blessed, or enviable. From makarizo; beatification, i.e. Attribution of good fortune.

3499.d: Lit. and met: I put to death, make as dead; I render weak, impotent. From nekros; to deaden, i.e. to subdue.

3500.d: (a) putting to death, (b) dead or lifeless condition. From nekroo; decease; figuratively, impotency.

3876.d: Disobedience, imperfect hearing. From parakouo; inattention, i.e. disobedience.

3922.d: To come in alongside, i.e. Supervene additionally or steathily.

3804.d: Something undergone, i.e. Hardship or pain; subjectively, an emotion or influence.

3611.d: To inhabit, dwell, indwell. From oikos; to occupy a house, i.e. Reside; by implication, to cohabit.

3873.d: To be at hand, be present with, rest with. From para and keimai; to lie near, i.e. Be at hand.

3601.d: Pain, sorrow, distress, of body or mind. From duno; grief.

3380.d: Not yet. From me and po; not yet.

3627.d: To pity, have compassion on. Also prolonged oiktereo oyk-ter-eh'-o from oiktos; to exercise pity.

3201.d: To blame, censure, find fault. Middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to blame.

3949.d: To provoke to anger, exasperate. From para and orgizo; to anger alongside, i.e. Enrage.

3005.d: A remnant, remainder. From leipo; a remainder.

3577.d: The back (of men or animals). Of uncertain affinity; the back.

3628.d: Pity, compassion, favor, grace, mercy. From oikteiro; pity.

3050.d: (a) reasonable, rational, (b) metaphorical, as contrasted with the literal. From logos; rational.

3011.d: A public servant, i.e. A functionary in the Temple or Gospel, or a worshipper or benefactor.

3773.d: Urbanus, a Christian in Rome, fellow-worker of Paul. Of Latin origin; Urbanus, a Christian.

3488.d: Narcissus, a resident of Rome. A flower of the same name, from narke; Narcissus, a Roman.

3969.d: Patrobas, a Christian in Rome. Perhaps a contraction for Patrobios; father's life; Patrobas, a Christian.

3517.d: Nereus, a Christian in Rome. Apparently from a derivative of the base of naus; Nereus, a Christian.

3652.d: Olympas, a Christian man in Rome. Probably a contraction from Olumpiodoros; Olympas, a Christian.

3472.d: Folly, absurdity, foolishness. From moros; silliness, i.e. Absurdity.

3981.d: Persuasive, enticing, skilful. From peitho; persuasive.

3345.d: To transfigure or disguise; figuratively, to apply.

3785.d: First person singular of a past tense of opheilo; I ought, i.e. oh that!

3807.d: A boy's guardian or tutor, a slave who had charge of the life and morals of the boys of a family, not strictly a teacher.

3402.d: An imitator, follower. From mimeomai; an imitator.

3639.d: Ruin, doom, destruction, death. From a primary ollumi; ruin, i.e. Death, punishment.

3060.d: A railer, reviler, abuser. From loidos; abusive, i.e. A blackguard.

3183.d: A drunkard. From methuo; tipsy, i.e. a sot.

3386.d: Let alone, much less, much more. From meti and ge; not at all then, i.e. Not to say.

3080.d: Dissolution, release; a loosing, divorce. From luo; a loosening, i.e., divorce.

3435.d: To soil, stain, pollute, defile, lit. and met. Probably from melas; to soil.

3348.d: To share or participate; by implication, belong to, eat.

3815.d: To play, sport (includes singing and dancing), play in the manner of children. From pais; to sport.

3644.d: A destroyer. From olothreuo; a ruiner, i.e., a venomous serpent.

3559.d: A warning, admonition, counsel. From nous and a derivative of tithemi; calling attention to, i.e. mild rebuke or warning.

3111.d: A meat-market, marketplace. Of Latin origin; a butcher's stall, meat market or provision-shop.

3740.d: As often as, as many times as. Multiple adverb from hos; how many times as.

3750.d: The sense of smell, smelling. From a derivative of ozo; smell.

3889.d: Encouragement, comfort, consolation, exhortation. From paramutheomai; consolation.

3515.d: To be childlike, childish, infantile. From nepios; to act as a babe, i.e. innocently.

3513.d: A particle of attestation; as sure as.

3786.d: Advantage, gain, profit, help. From ophello; gain.

3657.d: Intercourse, companionship, conversation, association. From homilos; companionship, i.e. intercourse.

3887.d: To remain by, abide with; met: I persevere in. From para and meno; to stay near, i.e. Remain.

3938.d: A passing by or through. From para and hodos; a by-road, i.e. a route.

3134.d: Maranatha, i.e. An exclamation of the approaching divine judgment.

3540.d: A perception, i.e. Purpose, or the intellect, disposition, itself.

3188.d: Ink. Neuter of melas as noun; ink.

3749.d: Made of clay, earthen. From ostrakon; earthen-ware, i.e. Clayey; by implication, frail.

3910.d: At the very instant, i.e. Momentary.

3613.d: A dwelling-place, habitation, abode. Neuter of a presumed derivative of oikeo; a residence.

3469.d: To blame, find fault with, slander. From momos; to carp at, i.e. Censure.

3352.d: Sharing, partnership, fellowship. From metecho; participation, i.e. Intercourse.

3841.d: Ruler of all, ruler of the universe, the almighty. From pas and kratos; the all-ruling, i.e. God.

3436.d: Staining, defilement, pollution. From moluno; a stain; i.e. immorality.

3993.d: One who works for his living; a laborer, poor man. From a primary peno; starving, i.e. Indigent.

3671.d: A profession, confession. From the same as homologeo; acknowledgment.

3794.d: A fortress, strong defense, stronghold. From a remote derivative of echo; a castle.

3999.d: Five times. Multiplicative adverb from pente; five times.

3489.d: To be shipwrecked, literally or figuratively.

3449.d: Wearisome labor, toil, hardship. From the base of mogis; toil, i.e. sadness.

3967.d: Ancestral, paternal, belonging to the fathers (ancestors). From pater; paternal, i.e. Ancestral.

3716.d: To be straight-footed, i.e. to go directly forward.

3445.d: To form, fashion, shape, mold. From the same as morphe; to fashion.

3988.d: Persuasion, conviction, a yielding to persuasion. From a presumed derivative of peitho; persuadableness, i.e. Credulity.

3456.d: To make mouths at, i.e. Ridicule.

3320.d: A middle wall, partition wall, barrier. From mesos and toichos; a partition.

3372.d: Length. Probably akin to megas; length length.

3950.d: Exasperation, wrath, irritation, indignation. From parorgizo; rage.

3473.d: Foolish talking. From a compound of moros and lego; silly talk, i.e. Buffoonery.

3067.d: A bath (of water, not the vessel), water for washing, washing. From louo; a bath, i.e., baptism.

3118.d: Long-timed, long-lived. From makros and chronos; long-timed, i.e. Long-lived.

3809.d: Tutorage, i.e. Education or training; by implication, disciplinary correction.

3823.d: Wrestling, a wrestling bout; hence: a struggle, fight, conflict, contest. From pallo; wrestling.

3890.d: Comfort, consolation, an exhortation, persuasion, encouragement. Neuter of paramuthia; consolation.

3897.d: Near to, nearly. Neuter of a compound of para and the base of plesion; close by, i.e. almost.

3637.d: An eight-day old person or act.

3171.d: Greatly, very much, vehemently. Adverb from megas; much.

3453.d: To initiate, instruct; pass: To be disciplined, learn (a lesson). From the base of musterion; to initiate, i.e. to teach.

3707.d: Visible. From horao; gazed at, i.e. capable of being seen.

3884.d: To deceive, beguile, reason falsely, mislead. From para and logizomai; to misreckon, i.e. Delude.

3437.d: A complaint, fault, blame. From memphomai; blame, i.e., a fault.

3931.d: Solace, consolation, comfort. From a compound of para and a derivative of agora; an address alongside, i.e., consolation.

3642.d: Faint-hearted, of small courage. From oligos and pshar; little-spirited, i.e. Faint-hearted.

3401.d: To imitate, follow. Middle voice from mimos; to imitate.

3454.d: An idle tale, fable, fanciful story. Perhaps from the same as mueo; a tale, i.e. Fiction.

3150.d: Vain speaking, foolish talking. From mataiologos; random talk, i.e. Babble.

3545.d: Lawfully, rightfully. Adverb from a derivative of nomos; legitimately.

3713.d: To stretch forth, mid: To hanker after, long for, be eager for, aspire to.

3504.d: Newly planted, i.e. a young convert.

3672.d: Admittedly, without controversy. Adverb of present passive participle of homologeo; confessedly.

3336.d: Participation, sharing in, receiving. From metalambano; participation.

3443.d: To leave alone (solitary), forsake. From monos; to isolate, i.e. Bereave.

3580.d: To entertain strangers, practice hospitality. From a compound of xenos and dechomai; to be hospitable.

3616.d: To manage a household. From oikodespotes; to be the head of a family.

3059.d: Reviling, abuse. From loidoros; slander or vituperation.

3866.d: A deposit, anything committed to one's charge or trust. From paratithemi; a deposit, i.e. trust.

3125.d: A grandmother. Of natural origin; a grandmother.

3718.d: From a compound of orthos and the base of tomoteros, to make a straight cut, i.e. to dissect correctly.

3368.d: Not at any time, never. From mede and pote; not even ever.

3200.d: A parchment leaf, perhaps for notes. Of Latin origin; a sheep-skin.

3023.d: A lion. A primary word; a |lion|.

3044.d: Linus, a Christian in Rome. Perhaps from linon; Linus, a Christian.

3711.d: Prone to anger, passionate. From orge; irascible.

3151.d: A vain, empty talker. From mataios and lego; an idle talker, i.e. A wrangler.

3626.d: A keeper-at-home, a housekeeper. From oikos and ouros; a stayer at home, i.e. Domestically inclined.

3685.d: To profit, benefit, help; mid: I have profit, derive benefit.

3172.d: (divine) majesty, greatness. From megas; greatness, i.e. divinity.

3010.d: Given to serving (ministration), ministering. From the same as leitourgeo; functional publicly; i.e. Beneficient.

3901.d: To flow by, i.e. carelessly pass.

3405.d: (lit: repayment of price or payment of price due), reward, due punishment. From misthapodotes; requital.

3898.d: Similarly, in like manner, likewise. Adverb from the same as paraplesion; in a manner near by, i.e. similarly.

3895.d: To fall aside, i.e. to apostatize.

3315.d: To mediate, interpose, give bail. From mesites; to interpose, i.e to ratify.

3549.d: To legislate, i.e. to have enactments injoined, be sanctioned.

3331.d: (a) change, transformation, (b) removal. From metatithemi; transposition, i.e. Transferral, disestablishment.

3728.d: The taking of an oath, an oath. From a compound of horkos and a derivative of omnuo; asseveration on oath.

3406.d: A rewarder. From misthoo and apodidomi; a renumerator.

3369.d: Not yet. From mede and po; not even yet.

3927.d: An alien alongside, i.e. A resident foreigner.

3645.d: To destroy, cause to perish. From olethros; to spoil, i.e. Slay.

3984.d: A trial, experiment, attempt. From the base of peran; a test, i.e. Attempt, experience.

3374.d: A sheep's (sometimes pig's) hide, sheepskin. From melon; a sheep-skin.

3692.d: A crevice (in a rock), a cave, an opening, hole. Probably from optanomai; a hole, i.e. Cavern; by analogy, a spring.

3509.d: A cloud; met: a dense crowd, a multitude, great company. Apparently a primary word; a cloud.

3591.d: (properly: bulk, mass, hence) a weight, burden, encumbrance. Probably from the same as agkale; a mass, i.e. Burden.

3643.d: To have little regard for, i.e. To disesteem.

3541.d: Illegitimate, base-born. Of uncertain affinity; a spurious or illegitimate son.

3347.d: Afterwards. From meta and epeita; thereafter.

3913.d: Madness, folly. From paraphroneo; insanity, i.e. Foolhardiness.

3393.d: Pollution, defilement; a stain. From miaino; foulness.

3769.d: A tail. Apparently a primary word; a tail.

3382.d: The thigh. Perhaps a primary word; a thigh.
